title: Being a musician as a way of life
summary: The trumpet, the embouchure and why one becomes a musician.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: When I was young it was like that. Anybody could get a job. Now kids are going to Julliard and God, these kids are coming out of the school playing better than the best in my day, and these kids are not getting anyplace. Being a musician -- you know, as I look back on it, it's a philosophy, a way of life, it's your total life. And you don't just go into music because this is another aspect of your life, you know. Now I'm a musician, now I'm a father, now I'm a husband, now I'm going up skiing in the country. You're a fulltime musician or you're not any -- it's your whole life.
My wife wanted to write an article "What it's like to be married to an embouchure."
(Laughter.)
"The whole day depends on how my husband's lips feel that day."
(Laughter.)

And it's not a joke. Your whole day -- you can get in the morning and the way your lip feels determines what the whole day's going to be like. I had one friend who quit music. "I don't want to be married to a goddamned trumpet." I said, well, if that's the way you feel, then get out of the business because unless you have a marriage, you should get a divorce.
I happen to enjoy being a musician. My greatest pleasure is practicing and playing. I'm not too crazy about listening to other musicians, unless there's something I can steal from them.
(Laughter.)
But otherwise, I don't much like to listen to others.
Spend that time accomplishing something yourself.

Yeah. So, you know, unless a kid -- like I tell my own students, you know, they say, should I be a musician? I say, no. They say, why do you say that? I say, because if you should, you would never ask me. If you don't --
That's a whole life.

You know, if you'd rather -- unless you want to starve as a musician rather than being pretty successful selling insurance or whatever you can get into, credit card salesman or something, then don't be a musician. You don't be a musician because you -- well, maybe you do because you want to be rich and famous, you think you're going to meet girls and whatever. You're a musician because if you weren't a musician there wouldn't be much point to your life. That's why you become a musician.
That's right. That's the way we feel about it, anyway. There's just no choice for me.
No.
It never occurred to me.

I didn't even think I was going to be a musician. I just didn't want to go to work on the railroad. I knew I loved to practice and copy records and play, and I just started playing, like this was what I was supposed to be doing. I kept thinking I was going to be a doctor some day. About three or four years ago I realized I'm never going to be a doctor, about the time I was 59 or 60.
(Laughter.)
In fact, I never even thought about it in the last 40 years.
(Recording interruption.)
